A UI export (save) only carries parameter values; it can’t be the graph.

wf.inspectTip: List the nodes this file has, and which are missing

roles.notGraphTitle: This file can’t be the submission graph
roles.notGraphBody: {reason}. Role mapping needs an API export: in ComfyUI’s menu pick Save (API Format) or Export (API), then point that file here.
roles.notGraphBodyBare: The node list can’t be read. Role mapping needs an API export: in ComfyUI’s menu pick Save (API Format) or Export (API), then point that file here.
roles.verdictOk: Roles are complete and the wires match — submissions use your graph
roles.verdictBad: Not ready yet (submissions will be refused)
roles.intro: Synco fills your graph by role, not by node id: moving things around or renumbering changes nothing. Point at the ones we can’t detect here; each file keeps its own mapping.

cloud.modelPh: Model name exactly as your provider gives it, e.g. gpt-image-2
cloud.modeCloudWhy: The route for machines without ComfyUI
cloud.runLocal: Generation still runs on local ComfyUI
cloud.ckLabel: Use cloud inpainting (tick this on a machine without ComfyUI)
cloud.ckNote: When ticked, submissions from the retouch page expand the mask, crop a region and send it to the cloud; the result is colour-corrected in the browser and stitched back with multiband blending — untouched pixels stay identical, so there’s no whole-image drift. Steps / CFG / LoRA / seed have no counterpart on this route and the panel hides them; the negative prompt is merged into the positive one. Batch submission doesn’t use the cloud yet.
cloud.baseLabel: base_url (the prefix your provider gives, including /v1)
cloud.sizeLabel: Default output long edge (overridable per submission)
cloud.stitchTitle: Stitching (raise these when the seam shows)
cloud.stitchNote: Expand = how many pixels wider the model repaints than your stroke; the seam hides in there. Feather = width of the blend-back band; 64 or more for smooth fabric and gradients. Feather is clamped to ≤ 0.6 × expand, so an over-large value is pulled back. Changes apply on the next submission.
cloud.clearKeyTip: Erase the key from the local database
cloud.keyNote: The key is written only to the local SQLite file, the service binds to loopback, and no endpoint sends it back to the page — but it is stored in plain text, so don’t sync the data folder anywhere.

setup.rootPh: The folder holding your ComfyUI portable pack, e.g. C:\...\ComfyUI_windows_portable
setup.needRoot: Fill in the ComfyUI root, then press “Self-check”.
setup.envQwenWhy: Your ComfyUI is too old — upgrading brings it
setup.envTip: No root folder yet: pick the root of a local ComfyUI portable pack, then run the check
setup.packsTitle: Third-party node packs (this pipeline uses only these two)
setup.deepTip: Hashes every local file and compares it to the baseline; takes about ten seconds
setup.scriptNote: It writes to data\setup\ — double-click install_comfyui.bat yourself. With no local ComfyUI pack it downloads and unpacks one (~4 GB, resumable, with progress), then clones the missing node packs, installs dependencies and checks every weight fingerprint. It won’t download weights for you: the list carries no download sources, so missing ones are reported by path and size only, and your files are left alone.
setup.changedWhy: Everything below belongs to the old folder; press “Save & self-check” to re-test the new path
setup.computing: Hashing — about ten seconds for 22 GB…
setup.mismatch: Some files differ from the baseline
setup.mismatchBody: {names}: possibly a different build or a damaged download
setup.pickRoot: Pick the ComfyUI portable pack root (it should contain ComfyUI and python_embeded)
setup.browseTip: Avoids typing the path — pasted paths often carry quotes or a trailing slash, and those fail existence checks
setup.rootNote: Remote backends can only be probed over HTTP; the folder check runs against this machine.

export.ready: Folder is there — “Export” writes straight to it
export.gone: This folder doesn’t exist right now (USB stick unplugged?), it will be re-checked and created on export
export.unset: Not set yet: pressing “Export” on the retouch page will point you here
export.title: Export folder (local)
export.pickTitle: Pick a folder for exported images
export.note: “Export” on the retouch page copies the current result here as `originalname_#id.png`, without going through the browser download; a missing folder is created. Writability is probed on every export, so an unplugged drive fails on the spot.

image.curLevelNote: Only originals with a long edge above {edge} get a proxy; thumbnails are 320 and tiles 512, fixed
image.afterChangeNote: The level is part of the file name, so old ones age out and new ones are cut lazily on first access — no manual cleanup
image.savedNote: Proxies are cut once the long edge passes {edge}
image.cacheNote: Tiles and everything the Local edit pass renders live in `data/runtime/cache/` — this layer can always be rebuilt. Originals, masks and the lossless masters are not part of it. Set the cap to 0 for no limit.
image.cacheClearText: Only tile and retouch caches go; the next look at that image re-renders them (about half a second for 24MP). Originals, masks and the files exports are built from stay put.
image.title: Editing level (proxy long edge)
image.note: Both the retouch canvas and the paint layer work at this level: lower saves memory and VRAM, higher lets you pick out detail on the original. The original always stays on disk; changing this never touches it.

data.pickNew: Pick a folder for the studio’s data
data.movedNote: Takes effect after restarting the studio; nothing in the old folder was touched
data.pickCopy: Copy the data into this folder (must be empty)
data.copiedNote: Open the new folder after restarting
data.formDesktop: Desktop · the UI is embedded in the exe
data.formWeb: Browser · the UI is read from {dir} on disk

data.shellDead: The shell side can’t be read
data.shellDeadNote: {why} (the folder, project count and size come from the shell, so those three rows are gone; the move and copy buttons stop working too)
data.needDesktopNote: This step needs the desktop build: open Synco.exe and the picker and copy buttons appear here
data.copyBtn: Copy the data to a new folder…
data.title: Where the data lives
data.note: Beyond hundreds of projects and tens of GB of weights, the studio’s own database and originals live only in this folder. The desktop build looks for an existing database nearby on first run; if it guesses wrong, change it here — you can just record the new address, or copy everything over.

theme.reduceLabel: Reduce motion (no page fades, no canvas gesture inertia, theme switches land instantly)
theme.title: Base colour
theme.note: Only the window, lists and panels change. The band around the canvas stays a neutral dark — judging colour needs a stable surround, so switching themes never pushes the photo warm or cool.
theme.motionAll: Motion: full (canvas inertia, page fades and theme crossfade are on)
theme.motionBoth: Motion: reduced (this switch and the system’s “reduce motion” are both on)
theme.motionOs: Motion: reduced (from the system’s “reduce motion” preference; leave this off to follow only the system)
theme.effectiveSys: In effect: {mode} (follows the system; changing its appearance switches immediately)
theme.motionNote: This is the same setting as the system’s “reduce motion”: either one on makes everything instant here. While on, theme switching has no crossfade (there was never one to keep), and the base colour still changes immediately.

ad.pushTip: Pushes pixels along the drag — pushing inward along a body contour slims it
ad.puckerTip: Pulls toward the disc centre; everything inside shrinks
ad.bloatTip: Swells outward from the centre; everything inside grows
ad.restoreTip: Pulls this area back to before any warp
ad.contrastTip: Scales around mid-grey, which barely moves
ad.highlightsTip: Acts on the bright end only
ad.shadowsTip: Acts on the dark end only
ad.tempTip: Positive = warmer: R up, B down
ad.tintTip: Positive = magenta: G down, B raised
ad.vibranceTip: Already-saturated areas get nothing; skin tone is protected first
ad.beautySharpenTip: One 3×3 high-frequency pass in the luma domain
ad.smoothTip: Bilateral filtering runs in a 2048 long-edge domain; the high frequency it removes is restored proportionally
ad.textureTip: The floor of the smoothing restore: 0 keeps its own curve, further right keeps more skin texture
ad.blemishTip: Only pulls back what clearly deviates from the local mean — spots, marks, stubble; normal texture stays
ad.evenToneTip: Moves chroma toward the large-scale layer to even out red/green patchiness. Skin only — sky and walls stay
ad.brightenTip: Brightens the skin range only; if sky or walls move along, it is broken
ad.deShineTip: Pushes skin highlights above the line (luma ≈185) back down; mid-tones below it stay
ad.fineRotTip: Small angles use bilinear resampling and the canvas grows to fit
ad.fillEdgeTip: Introduces no new colour — the least visible in a frame
ad.fillAvgTip: For letterboxing; averages the four source corners
ad.cropApplyTip: Previews the current frame · the original is untouched
ad.ratioHint: Aspect ratio · tap one and the crop frame appears
ad.pressureTip: One step moves at most 45% of the radius; beyond that it bites into its own previous sample
ad.warpNote: While dragging, only the disc area shows the client’s approximation; on release the whole parameter chain recomputes and the server’s image is authoritative.
ad.lutStrengthTip: How much is mixed with the original; 0 = no LUT at all
ad.byMaskTip: Reuses the mask strokes: smooth where you painted; off means the whole image
ad.maskNote: No mask = whole image. This layer’s mask lives in the post-warp domain.
ad.footNote: The original is never rewritten: everything below is parameters and can be rolled back any time. Previews run at the proxy level; only rendering uses full resolution.
ad.presetNote: A built-in preset is a set of slider values — tapping one moves those sliders
ad.noLastCrop: Nothing has been cropped this session, so there is no “last” to go back to
ad.tilesBusy: Computing this version at true pixels…
ad.cropHint: Drag the frame over what to keep · press “✔ Crop this” to see the result
ad.warpHint: Drag with “{brush}” on the canvas · middle button pans
ad.emptyStroke: This stroke never left a path, so nothing was recorded
ad.clearBody: This image has {n} strokes. Clearing returns it to crop/colour only; the original is unaffected.
ad.noChange: No slider moved, so there is nothing to render
ad.rendered: Result rendered ({ms} ms) · the original stayed
ad.renderedReuse: These parameters were rendered before; the file was reused
ad.noChangeFork: Nothing is adjusted yet, so saving a new image would be pointless
ad.forking: Rendering and registering a new image…
ad.forkedBody: The new image starts with empty parameters; this adjustment set stays on the parent
ad.forkFailTitle: Couldn’t save as a new image
ad.clearAllBody: Crop, strokes, colour and beauty all return to unadjusted and the view goes back to the source. The original was never modified — clearing just stops stacking these parameters.
ad.cleared: Cleared — back to the source image
ad.geomLocked: After a crop or rotation the image and the mask aren’t in one coordinate system: apply as a new image before painting again
ad.presetTip: A preset is a set of slider values ({id})

pm.promptPh: Describe what to change — one subject and one action per sentence
pm.chipMgrTip: Add, edit or remove these phrases
pm.cloudNote: Cloud mode: the negative prompt is merged into the positive one, and there are no steps / CFG / LoRA / seed to tune.
pm.edgeUseSetting: Uses the long edge set in Settings

pm.cfgTip: Higher follows the prompt more closely; too high smears
pm.seedTip: Used when the random seed is off
pm.randSeedTip: A fresh seed on every submission while on
pm.batchNote: In a batch each image adds its index to the seed, so nothing repeats yet the shots stay comparable.
pm.loraNote: Switches and strengths rewrite the Lora chain at submit time; turning one off takes it off the model chain.
pm.noLora: The workflow has no LoRA attached.
pm.modeCloudTip: The cloud repaints the whole cropped region
pm.inkPartTip: Repaints inside the strokes and keeps the original outside
pm.inkKeepTip: Enclose the subject; everything else is repainted
pm.inkFullTip: Ignores the mask: the whole original is sent and generated from the prompt, so pixels outside the mask are no longer preserved
pm.inkKeepNote: Everything else goes to the cloud
pm.inkFullNote: The whole image is sent; no original pixels are kept
